scope.content: Revised Obstacle and wall avoidance record/model/spec and the provenance expansion in the twenty WO-028 study bylines.
scope.exclusions: No broader implementation review, browser or drawing-readability judgment, tests, gates, dependency installation, repository mutation or background work.

summary: F4's default now demonstrates a successful glancing avoidance manoeuvre, and F5's twenty expanded bylines agree with the retained author assignments. One medium content finding remains: named moments claim a hit or turn that some offered inputs never produce.

findings.claim: The named moments Ray first hits and Turning along the wall identify events in the currently selected run.
reproduction: Keep every record parameter at its default except set the offered rayLength input to 0.5 (1 also reproduces). The independent scalar simulation finds no ray/wall intersection in all 81 frames. firstHit and turning therefore both equal -1.
The model nevertheless maps both event labels to step 0. At that step the ray is (0,0) to (0.5,0), the wall is at x=10, the frame truthfully says no hit, and acceleration seeks delivery (18,15).

A second reproduction is offered goalY=0 with rayLength=9. Every position and acceleration has y=0; the turning predicate is never true. Turning along the wall nevertheless points to the first-hit step 3 (0.3 s), whose acceleration is (8,0).
findings.impact: The event controls contradict the selected frame and teach an event that did not occur when the reader explores explicitly offered inputs.
findings.boundedCorrection: Omit unavailable event moments or give their fallback a truthful label such as Start of run / No ray hit in this run. Do not call a fallback frame a turn. Recheck the no-hit case and the straight-on case as well as the default.

defaultAndTurning.independentMethod: A fresh Python scalar implementation read only record parameters, implemented the finite-segment equations, engine Seek formula and speed-capped semi-implicit update; it imported no model or engine code. Exact point/segment and segment/segment distances checked the continuous straight travel between fixed-step positions.
defaultAndTurning.explanation: The normal-offset target supplies a stronger sideways acceleration than the delivery pull at the hit. Hits occur at frames 5 and 6; from frame 7 the forward ray clears the upper endpoint and delivery steering resumes. This is a local turn, not a planned route.
defaultAndTurning.caution: The displayed minimum is computed over plotted samples. The independent swept minimum has the same rounded default value and remains positive.

straightOnComparison.unchanged: Initial position/velocity, radius, ray length 9, offset 6, speed, acceleration and integration.
straightOnComparison.explanation: The run brakes, reverses and repeatedly switches between the avoidance and delivery target on the same line. It remains on the approach side and supplies no side-selection or route policy. Floating-point near-zero velocity is retained rather than treated as an invented exact stop.

checks: The cross-product fractions intersect two finite segments; both fractions must be in [0,1]. The selected normal is unit length and opposes the incoming ray. A zero denominator deliberately rejects both parallel and collinear cases.
The clearance formula uses nearest=(wallX, clamp(y, wallBottom, wallTop)); its Euclidean distance minus radius is valid on either side and around both endpoints for this vertical wall.

Endpoint checks independently give clearance 1 at (12,0), 1 at (10,8), sqrt(0.5)-1 at (9.5,6.5), and -1 at (10,0). A horizontal centre ray from (9.5,6.5) misses despite the disc overlapping the upper endpoint.

The four ordinary pseudocode blocks agree with the four mechanism steps and the code: detect, select target, call engine Seek, measure then advance using the newly capped velocity. Last travel heading is retained only at exactly zero speed.
The hand-worked head-on state at x=4.4, vx=4, target=(4,0) gives acceleration=(-8,0), next vx=3.2, next x=4.72 and current clearance=4.6.
The model's chart, text-equivalent keys and worked arithmetic describe the same state and target. No hidden wall clamp or collision response appears in the update.

offeredInputsAndLimits.result: limits are genuine; FC-01 concerns their event controls
offeredInputsAndLimits.parameterGrid: All 456 combinations offered by goalY=0..18 by 1 and rayLength=0.5..12 by 0.5, over 81 positions each.
observations: Changing only default rayLength to 1 produces no hit and actual upper-end disc overlap: plotted minimum -0.082825280 and between-update minimum -0.086086834. The short-ray limitation is visible in the offered default situation.

At the rayLength endpoints with goalY=15, 0.5 gives no hit and between-update clearance -0.086086834; 12 gives hits but clearance -0.739523397. Longer detection is not a universal clearance guarantee.
At the goalY endpoints with rayLength=9, goalY=0 stays on the centre line with minimum clearance 3.8, while goalY=18 clears with between-update minimum 0.870216037.

At combined extremes (goalY, rayLength)=(0,0.5), the centre crosses the wall and clearance reaches -1 between updates; (0,12) remains straight with minimum 3.8; (18,0.5) has no hit and minimum 0.767963517; (18,12) clips the upper endpoint with minimum -0.005407915.

These overlaps are legitimate exposed limitations of a centre ray plus local target steering, not findings that every slider setting must avoid collision. The source and record make no such guarantee.

The corner-trap claim is scoped to multiple rays and adjacent faces, not presented as executed by this one-wall model. Seek is not Arrive; the model also does not promise to settle at the destination.

The public vector operations provide arithmetic, unit vectors, distance, dot product and updated-velocity speed clipping.
local: Finite ray/wall intersection and selection of a normal opposite travel.
Normal-offset avoidance target and delivery fallback.
